name.text: Solving a linear inequality requiring a sign reversal

questiontext.text:
Solve the following inequality for \(x\):

\( \displaystyle {@a@} - {@b*x@} > {@c@} \)

(Enter your answer as an inequality. Use < for less than and > for greater than. For example, x < 5)

Equation: [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

To solve the inequality, we need to isolate \(x\).

First, we group the constant terms on the right side by subtracting \({@a@}\) from both sides.

\( \displaystyle \begin{aligned} -{@b*x@} &> {@c@} - ({@a@}) \\ -{@b*x@} &> {@c - a@} \end{aligned} \)

Next, we divide both sides by \(-{@b@}\).

Crucial Rule: Because we are dividing by a negative number, we must reverse the inequality sign.

\( \displaystyle \begin{aligned} x &< \frac{{@c - a@}}{-{@b@}} \\ x &< {@x_val@} \end{aligned} \)

Hence, the correct solution for this inequality is:

\( \displaystyle \boxed{x < {@x_val@}} \)

On a number line, the solution \(x < {@x_val@}\) is an open circle at \({@x_val@}\) with the line going to the left:

questiondescription.text:
This question is based on the example 15 - 2x >= 7 (dividing by a negative number reverses the sign) in the section Simple Inequalities of the CBC Grade 11 Mathematics textbook (INNODEMS).

Simple Inequalities (Negative Coefficients)

node.description: Check if they forgot to flip the sign

truefeedback.text: Your numerical value is correct, but you have the wrong inequality sign. Remember: When you divide both sides of an inequality by a negative number, you must reverse the inequality symbol.
